title: [Pre Order] Retroid Pocket Duo Handheld 8GB+128GB US$249 + US$25 Delivery (~A$382 Delivered) @ Retroid
body:
Deal: [Pre Order] Retroid Pocket Duo Handheld 8GB+128GB US$249 + US$25 Delivery (~A$382 Delivered) @ Retroid

[t0087669] Ordered lite.
The game play video showed played Zelda OoT with 2x resolution.
Will be interesting with continue improvement of emulation / software support, maybe more 3ds games can be played
[TheDukeOfNukem] I have had my 2DS in the drawer for aaaaages, lent it to a friend a while back so they could burn through some of the Pokemons on it without having to pay the insane prices they go for these days. Now, of course, despite not playing that unit in forever, I have an itch. Perfect timing for Retroid here.
[TheDukeOfNukem] Because then I wouldn't be getting a stupid new toy.
But also, we all know the second that little door stop of a console is back in my hands, I'll fire up the homebrew version of Doom for 5 minutes, maybe do a couple Mario Kart races and then when I don't get first in one, I'll turn the unit off, put it back in the drawer, and not see it for another few years.
[AustriaBargain] @TheDukeOfNukem: Yeah my house is full of things filled with much promise that I haven't turned on in years.
[cobknob] @AustriaBargain: You know batteries don't last? and even with charging it every 1-2x months they still won't last past a decade..
[BusMan247] @cobknob: My regular DS still chops ok original battery despite going through a 4 year didn’t know it existed period.
[AustriaBargain] @cobknob: Can still buy batteries for them, even some well regarded brands.
[gcheap] Yeah the Lite will have some decent 3DS potential for lighter titles and native/low upscale. The inline triggers are a big selling point for the Lite.
[TheDukeOfNukem] I never really play with upscalers (at least not too high) anyway. I've even played on .25/.5 upscale for some real low end PS2 shit. Frankly, for me, half the fun is in pushing the machine as far as I can.
Definitely agree about the triggers too! Lost my N3DSXL almost ten years ago (I still believe my then one year old kiddo left it outside and an opportunistic person walking Maroondah Hwy grabbed it), and those buttons alone are more nostalgic than the two screens to me.
[TheDukeOfNukem] Damn, this was sold out a few hours ago when I looked, cheers for the heads up, boss.
*Note, to everyone else: This preorder deal gets a "cheers" instead of a "not a deal" because there's an actual (profanity) discount code included. OzRRP can suck my (profanity)

[dottjt] Correct me if I'm wrong, but those CPU specs are worse than the RP6?
[RichardL] You are correct.
The RP6 has the Snapdragon 8 Gen 2.
The Nova has the Qualcomm Dragonwing QCS8550 (Snapdragon 8 Gen 2 without Cellular).
Both are better than the the CPU in the Pocket Duo - Qualcomm Dragonwing Q-7790 (Snapdragon 7 Gen 4 without Cellular).
I suspect they went with a weaker chipset to keep price lower and not to cannibalise the sales of the AYN Thor (same parent company).

But, be mindful, the early adopters of the retroid flip and flip 2 both had hinge issues.
I can only hope for everyone third time is the charm.
[cobknob] CPU: 1 A720@2.6GHz | 4 A720@2.4GHz | 3*A520@1.8GHz
What's with the 1x core @2.6GHz? Systems usually have 2,2,4 or 2,6 or 4,4 configs for an octo core chip
[tmr3] Lots of examples of Snapdragon SoCs with single "prime" cores of some fashion (can be just a higher clocked "mid" core or an actual "prime" core depending on the SoC). It's been a bit of a staple for quite some time in the Snapdragon 7-series which the chip in the Duo is based on.
7 Gen 1 (2022): 1x A710 @ 2.4 GHz
7+ Gen 2 (2023): 1x X2 @ 2.91 GHz
7 Gen 3 (2023): 1x A715 @ 2.63 GHz
7+ Gen 3 (2024): 1x X4 @ 2.8 GHz
7s Gen 3 (2024): 1x A720 @ 2.5 GHz
7 Gen 4 (2025): 1x A720 @ 2.8 GHz (which this Dragonwing Q-7790 is based on)
7s Gen 4 (2025): 1x A720 @ 2.7 GHz
Beyond that, lots of older 800-series SoCs (855, 855+, 860, 865, 865+, 870, 888, 888+ all with 1+3+4), as well as 8-series SoCs prior to the introduction of Oryon as well (8 Gen 1, 8+ Gen 1, 8 Gen 2, 8 Gen 3, 8s Gen 3, and 8s Gen 4 all with 1+3+4 configs)
[tmr3] Worth reminding anyone who is thinking of placing a pre-order that it could take upwards of two months to receive your order. YMMV.
I pre-ordered a Retroid Pocket Nova in clear purple on day one (27/6) and received it on Monday (7/9). Retroid maintains a sort of "shipment dashboard" which is a table of SKUs and colour options, along with which pre-order dates have been sent out and the last shipment date.
It took them two months just to ship out the first clear purple units while some other options had seen shipments for orders in August. For reference, Retroid claimed they would rotate through a day or two of manufacturing each colour, and have all pre-orders for the Nova shipped within three weeks.
The only other source of updates is their Discord server, but they're few and far between (and mainly seem to come from community volunteers rather than staff?).
I will say the new 4:3 OLED screen (bottom screen on the Duo) is really quite good so long as you're not a stickler for oversaturation. I can't really fault the quality of the product, just go in with low expectations for when you'll get your order and hopefully you'll be surprised.
[4agte] What advantages does this duo have over, say, a apple? Which I could also afford.
